PART VI SALT MIST TEST

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part VI ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 16 August 1982,after the draft finalized by the Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 Fast development in the field of instruments has brought a significant It has been felt over the years change in their basic content and design. that IS : 2352-19631i does not cater for the present day needs of the instruments and is also not in line with the recent trends in climatic and environmental testing procedures to be adopted for improving their It has, therefore, become necessary to have quality and reliability. uniform and more rational testing procedures as far as possible. This series of standards on climatic and durability tests ( IS : 10236 ) has been prepared with this objective. 0.2.1 It is .proposed to withdraw the existing Indian Standard ( IS : 2352-1963* ) as soon as the tests mentioned therein are covered in the new series ( IS : 10236 ).

3.1 The object of this test is to determine the suitability of optical instruments for use or storage in a salt laden atmosphere as available in coastal areas or sea crafts. 4. INITIAL 4.1 The MEASUREMENTS

instrument shall be visually examined and checked optically, electrically and mechanically as required by the relevant instrument specification.

5. TEST 5.1 The

CHAMBER
used for this test shall meet the requirements given

chamber in 5.1.1 to 5.1.7.

5.1.1 The chamber materials which shall the salt mist.

and ail its internal fittings shall be made of not be adversely affected by the corrosive effect of

5.1.2 The chamber shall have two separate compartments, the lower one for producing fine spray and the upper for placing or hanging the instrument. The compartments shall be SO inter-connected that the spray produced in lower part fills the atmosphere of the upper part with salt laden fine mist without any direct impingement of spray on the instrument. 5.1.3 The salt spray shall be produced by an atomizer employing compressed air which must be free from all impurities. The spray mechanism shall have provision of adjusting air pressure such that the solution sprayed per hour is approximately one percent of the volume of the chamber. 5.1.4 The chamber shall be properly up inside the chamber. vented to prevent pressure buildshall be and the

5.1.5 The cover, the walls and all other parts of the chamber so arranged that no condensate drips on the test instrument instrument does not come into contact with any'metal part.

5.1.6 For each spraying cycle a fresh supply of salt solution shall be used. Also during each cycle the solution once sprayed shall not be allowed to return to salt solution reservoir. 5.1.7 The the storage atmosphere. salt mist chamber or a humidity chamber shall be used for of the instrument under test after exposure to saline The chamber used for this purpose shall be capable of 4

8.5 The instrument shall then be stored at a temperature of 35 & 2?C and relative humidity 90 to 95 percent for a period of 22 hours, in case of severity I and VII days in case of severity II. 8.6 The above exposure and storage shall constitute one cycle. The instrument shall be subjected to the number of cycles appropriate to the severity I or II or as specified in the relevant instrument specification. 8.7 The instrument shall then be removed from the chamber and cleaned using tap water, unless otherwise specified by the relevant instrument specification. The instrument shall then be dried for one hour at 55 &- 2�C. 8.8 Recovery - The instrument shall then be allowed to cool under the standard atmospheric conditions for recovery for not less than one hour nor more than two hours. 9. FINAL MEASUREMENTS

9.1 After recovery the instrument shall be visually examined for the evidence of any corrosion and deterioration of metal parts, finish, materials and components. Its performance shall also be checked in accordance with the relevant instrument specification. 10. DETAILS TO BE SPECIFICATION GIVEN IN RELEVANT INSTRUMENT

10.1 When this test is included in the relevant instrument specification the following details shall be given as far as applicable for carrying out this test: a) Initial observations'measurements, b) Test severity, c) Duration of storage after exposure if other than specified, d) Cleaning after test, e) Final observations/measurements, and f) Any deviation from the normal procedure.
